responses.sql: SELECT e.status, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: An attendee is counted as one attendance row (event, member pair), so a member attending several events is counted once per event. The share is the status's count divided by the total of matched attendance rows across all statuses, as a fraction between 0 and 1 and not a percentage.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct members per status, so a member who attended several events of the same status is counted once. The share is that count divided by the sum of the per-status distinct counts.
alternatives.sql: SELECT e.status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendee_count, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.status

responses.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(*) AS attendees, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: Each matched attendance row (event, member) counts as one attendee, so attendees per status = number of attendance rows; a member attending several events with the same status is counted once per event.
Share is a fraction (0 to 1) of the total matched attendance rows across all statuses, left unrounded.
Events with NULL status form their own group and count in the total.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct members per status (a member attending several events of the same status is counted once); share is relative to the sum of these per-status distinct counts.
alternatives.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attendees, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status

responses.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: Attendees are counted as attendance rows (event, member pairs) that match an event; since the primary key is (event, member), each row is one attendance, so a member attending events in several events is counted once per event.
Share is a fraction between 0 and 1 (count divided by total matched attendance rows), not a percentage, and is left unrounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct members per status (a member who attended several events of the same status counts once), with share relative to the sum of those per-status distinct counts.
alternatives.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) AS attendee_count, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member)) OVER () AS share FROM (SELECT e.status AS status, a.link_to_member AS link_to_member FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event) GROUP BY status
